text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm working on the audit-log docs to add example queries and a short migration snippet for the new export endpoint. Need a quick review on SOC2-safe language and whether the query examples we show are acceptable (we currently include a timestamp filter and a minimal event payload). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1482
eli: SG — can you paste the example you're planning to include?
maya: Sure, here's the current sample we added (meant to be copy-paste friendly for clients):
```http
GET /audit-logs?start=2023-12-01T00:00:00Z&end=2023-12-31T23:59:59Z&event_type=access
Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
```
And example response snippet:```json
{
  "events": [
    {"ts":"2023-12-07T14:22:10Z","user_id":"u_123","event":"api_key.used","resource":"model:abc"},
    {"ts":"2023-12-10T09:11:05Z","user_id":"u_456","event":"export.started","resource":"audit:export_202312"}
  ]
}
```
eli: That response example is good as-is — it avoids any PII (user_id is an internal id), which is safer for public docs. For SOC2 language: avoid implying we surface raw PII in the audit stream. Maybe add a callout: "Audit logs record security-relevant events; any user-identifying values are internal identifiers and redacted when required."
tom: On the SDK migration snippet — the export endpoint changed signature; I drafted a JS snippet for the docs that uses the new client method:```js
// old: client.audit.export({from, to})
// new:
const res = await client.audit.createExport({
  filter: {from: '2023-12-01', to: '2023-12-31', event_types: ['access']},
  destination: {type: 's3', bucket: 'acme-audit-exports'}
});
console.log(res.export_id);
```
I want to make sure we don't show credentials or bucket names. Use placeholders.
sara: Small wording nit: instead of "createExport" maybe use `startExport` to match the REST verb (POST /audit-exports). If it's a breaking name change we should call it out in migration section. Also add a tiny note about RBAC: only org admins can create exports.
maya: Good call, I'll rename to `startExport` and add the RBAC note. Any compliance wording suggestions? We were going to say "retention settings determine how long events are retained" — is that too loose for SOC2?
eli: For SOC2, be concrete where possible. E.g., "Retention settings control the retention period for audit events; your organization can configure retention per-organization and data type. Redwood does not surface raw PII in audit log exports unless explicitly included by customer configuration." Keep it short.
sara: Also add an example of a time-range filter query and show timezone handling — people trip up on Z vs local offsets. Suggest adding: `start=2023-12-01T00:00:00Z` note: all timestamps in examples are UTC.
maya: Will add. One more: link break in the Console -> Audit page docs — the anchor changed after that last restructure. The PR currently points to /console/audit#exporting but the site uses /console/audit#exports now. Can someone confirm?
tom: Yep the anchor is `#exports`. I'll add a small linkfix commit.
security-bot: Reminder: per policy, do not include example payloads that contain full emails, SSNs, or other high-risk data. Use internal ids or masked values.
eli: Approving the content approach. Two small asks: 1) add short sample curl for export POST (no creds) and 2) add an explicit "Examples are illustrative" disclaimer before the code blocks.
maya: Got it. I'll add the curl, the timezone note, the RBAC sentence, rename to `startExport`, fix the link, and add the SOC2-appropriate callout. I'll push an updated commit in ~30m and ping again. Thanks all :thumbsup:
tom: Thanks — small follow-up after your update: can we also add a short line about retention auditability (how to view retention policy changes in the audit logs)? A one-liner and a link to the retention policy doc should be enough.
maya: Good idea. I'll add: "Retention policy changes are recorded in the audit log as policy.update events; see retention docs for details."
eli: Awesome. No further blockers from me.
security-bot: Automated check: PR 1482 flagged a missing docs link to compliance matrix. Suggested link: /docs/compliance/soc2-matrix.
maya: Thanks — adding that link now. Will update the PR so the build passes.
eli: Cool, thanks for driving this.
maya: Update pushed — PR now includes: timezone note, RBAC line, startExport JS + curl examples, linkfix to #exports, compliance matrix link, and the SOC2-safe callout. Marking this thread resolved for now.
security-bot: PR 1482: link checks passed on updated commit.
